sentences.text: M E N T / Awar D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)

1.  This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after LAC no. 38/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Ram Phal v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 15 completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.

The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.

6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.

The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly LAC no. 38/
2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Phal v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 15 inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

entities.text: Ram Phal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 14.09.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been LAC no. 38/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Ram Phal v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 15 taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

entities.text: Ram Phal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the Ram Phal (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174884132/
3 market value.

sentences.text: Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without LAC no. 38/
2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Phal v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 15 adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

sentences.text: The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,
which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.
( vi )
The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2 3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the LAC no. 38/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Ram Phal v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 15 concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Mubarakpur Dabas and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.

entities.text: Ram Phal v. Union of India

sentences.text: The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

The petitioners are also claiming value of the trees admitted Rs. 1000 per quintal and compensation for the standing crops @ Rs. 1 lakh, compensation of Well @ Rs. 2 lakhs, compensation of tubewell @ Rs. 5 lakhs and the value of the room @ Rs. 2 lakhs per room and other statutory benefits.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted the Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for the year 2001 - 2002,
which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
The Ld. LAC adopted the indicative price fixed by the Government of NCT of Delhi of land falling in "Block A".

As far as the land having ghadda upto 23 feet, the ld. LAC has deducted Rs. 1,70,000 per acre from the market value of "Block B" category land, therefore, after deduction the value comes to Rs. 14,00,000 per acre, and as such the market value of the said land was assessed as per the rate prevailing during the corresponding period for LAC no. 38/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))

It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.

11. It is submitted that the said land was taken over by DDA on 04.04.2006 and 03.01.2007 after acquisition the possession of the land, the same was subsequently handed over to RPD VII.

18. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

20. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/

There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
